<thought>To meet the constraints, I verified the commercial availability of all leaf reagents. The only non‑buyable reagent in the original Mitsunobu step was DIAD. I replaced the Mitsunobu ether formation with a straightforward Williamson ether synthesis using a brominated side‑chain that already contains the required internal hydroxyl group (OCC=CC=CCBr). This bromide is commercially available, and the subsequent oxidation of its terminal alcohol to the carboxylic acid completes the side‑chain functionality. All other reagents (4‑methylcyclohex‑1‑ene, acetyl chloride, pyridine, NaH, NaOH, NaClO, etc.) are buyable, and the total cost is far below $10 000. The route uses exactly five steps and each leaf is a commercially available chemical.</thought>
